primary_task: Migrate the Swift side of an existing Apple Expo native module from the Expo Modules API 1.0 DSL to the 2.0 macro API, preserving the JS/TS contract, and verify it builds and the example app resolves the module.

requirements.name: macOS with Xcode / Apple Swift toolchain (iOS SDK, CocoaPods)
requirements.evidence: Step 4 'Verify behavior': '1. Build or type-check the Apple module against the target `expo-modules-core`.' ... '3. Build and launch the example app when the repository provides one.' ... 'restart Xcode before diagnosing plugin communication failures.' and 'the example app must actually resolve the module, not merely compile.'
requirements.basis: lacks: 'Windows or macOS, and their GUI toolchains (Xcode, Visual Studio, PowerShell on Windows)'; description: 'A Claude Code cloud session on Linux x86_64'.

requirements.name: npm / node (npm ls expo, expo 57.0.21+)
requirements.evidence: Prerequisite: 'check the target's installed version (`expo` in `package.json`/lockfile, or `npm ls expo`)'
requirements.basis: bash: 'install packages from the open registries (pip from PyPI, npm, apt from Ubuntu, go modules, nuget, GitHub release downloads)'.

requirements.name: read/edit source files (Swift, expo-module.config.json)
requirements.evidence: 'Migrate the Swift side of an existing Expo module'; '### 3. Apply the migration'
requirements.basis: tools: 'read: read files in the working directory' and 'edit: edit existing files'.

requirements.name: gh issue create --repo expo/expo (tracking issue)
requirements.evidence: 'Open a tracking issue on `expo/expo` ... Use `gh issue create --repo expo/expo` and confirm with the user before posting' (only when a 2.0 equivalent is missing)
requirements.basis: forbid_effects: 'writes_external' (posting an outward issue); conditional, so not hard.

requirements.name: npx submit-expo-feedback
requirements.evidence: 'Only submit when you have something specific and actionable to report.' (npx --yes submit-expo-feedback@latest ...)
requirements.basis: npm is open but the feedback endpoint host is not named in the manifest ('other hosts are refused'); optional.

notes: Reading taken: the numbered step 4 (build the Apple module, launch the example app, warning that a stale module entry only fails at runtime) is part of the deliverable, so an Apple toolchain is required. Other reading: if the primary task is only the source rewrite (steps 1-3) and verification is secondary, the verdict would be ACHIEVABLE (unverified on Linux). The rewrite itself needs only read/edit.
